title: Wake the Terminal
concept: C01 · Semicolons end statements; C# is case-sensitive
given: // Print a greeting to the terminal

decoys.why: CS0103: the name 'console' does not exist. Case matters: it is Console.
CS1002: ; expected. A colon is not a semicolon.

review: Mistake #1 and #2 in one level. A good first-day warm-up.

decoys.why: CS0103: the name 'Mira' does not exist. Without quotes C# looks for a variable.
CS1012: too many characters in character literal. Single quotes are for one char.

title: Start the Score
concept: C02 · A variable must be given a value before it is used

decoys.why: CS0165: use of unassigned local variable 'score'. It was declared but never given a value.
CS0029: cannot convert string to int.

review: The castle wins only after = 0; an early ; triggers CS0165 on line 2.

decoys.why: CS0029: cannot implicitly convert int to bool. = stores a value; == asks a question.
Runs, but prints nothing: health is 0, not below 0.
Runs, but prints HP: {hp}. Without $ the braces are just text.
CS1003: syntax error, ',' expected. Join text and values with + or use $.

title: Count the Gold
concept: C02 · + joins text left to right

decoys.why: Runs, but prints Gold: 12. Once text is on the left, every + glues text.
CS0019: operator - cannot be applied to string and int.

title: Leftover Potions
concept: C02 · int division drops the remainder; % keeps it

decoys.why: Runs, but left is 3. That is how many each player gets, not what is left.
Runs, but left is 5.

review: int only, so it stays inside the GAME 220 ceiling.

title: Only the Living Heal
concept: C02 · A ; after if ends the if

decoys.why: Compiles (warning CS0642: possible mistaken empty statement), but Heal() now runs every time, even at hp 0.
CS0029: cannot convert int to bool.

review: Two-card answer; the third light auto-succeeds.

title: The Menu That Fell Through
concept: C03 · Every switch case needs break

decoys.why: CS0163: control cannot fall through from one case label to another. End the case with break;
Compiles inside the menu loop, but jumps straight back to the menu instead of ending the turn.

title: The Healer's Promise
concept: C03 · A method with a return type must return

decoys.why: CS0161: not all code paths return a value. Printing is not returning.
Runs, but Heal(20) returns 10. Wrong direction.

review: 4-card answer. Players must not stop at "return hp;" — that is legal but returns 20.

title: The Endless Shop
concept: C03 · A loop must change what it tests

decoys.why: Infinite loop: gold never changes. The castle times out.
Runs, but the loop never starts: gold stays 0.

review: 2-card answer in 4 slots; the two spare lights auto-succeed. Needs a "castle times out" outcome.

title: Take the Hit
concept: C05 · Call a method on the object

decoys.why: CS0120: an object reference is required. Player is the class; player is your hero.
CS1501: no overload for TakeDamage takes 2 arguments. (C05 demo)

title: The Hit That Did Nothing
concept: C05 · Update the field, do not declare a new variable
given:
class Player { int hp = 30;
  void TakeDamage(int amount) { ? } }

decoys.why: CS0165: use of unassigned local variable 'hp'. int makes a NEW hp that hides the field.
Runs, but hp becomes 10: it was replaced, not reduced.

title: Count the Loot
concept: C06 · Arrays start at 0 and end at Length - 1

decoys.why: IndexOutOfRangeException: items[3] does not exist. Runtime crash!
Runs, but prints Rope three times.

review: 4-card answer, a whole loop. C06 demo. Needs a "runtime crash" outcome.

title: The Empty Room
concept: C07 · Objects must be created with new, before use
given:
class World { Room inn;
  void Start() { ? } }

decoys.why: NullReferenceException: inn is still null when line 1 runs. Order matters!
Runs, but makes a NEW local inn. The world's inn field is still null (same trap as Q13).

review: 2-card answer where ORDER is the puzzle. The most common runtime crash.
